policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV EZK.22.18 renders the word twice as 'dross' ('is become dross unto me', 'the dross of silver'), with no ASV note mapped to this unit. The qere spelling לְסִיג and the ketiv לסוג are orthographic variants of the same noun for dross, so the English wording cannot distinguish them; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
